neighbours.label: a noun naming a hidden or hard-to-reach environment used as a setting or habitat (deep sea, gut, orbit, underground, the brain)
fire: Strange fish live in the deep ocean where no light reaches.
Researchers mapped the bacteria living in the human gut.
The telescope has spent twenty years in orbit around Earth.
Miners worked for weeks in tunnels deep underground.
Tiny worms survive near vents on the sea floor.
Few organisms can survive in the upper atmosphere.
Fungi spread through the soil beneath the forest floor.
Signals travel across the brain in a fraction of a second.
quiet: Strange fish live in the shop window near the market.
Researchers mapped the bacteria living on kitchen counters.
The telescope has spent twenty years in a museum in London.
Miners worked for weeks in offices in the city centre.
Tiny worms survive in garden compost all year.
Few organisms can survive in a clean hospital ward.
Fungi spread across the bread on the kitchen table.
Signals travel across the office in a fraction of a second.

notes: Card: peaks on ' gut' (bacteria), ' sea' (deep sea), ' orbit', ' underground', ' brain', ' meters' (depth). Shared pattern: an environment below or beyond ordinary reach. Near misses use ordinary everyday settings in the same sentence frames.
